bh-p01.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person vandana)
bh-p01.question: What is the object of veneration, and how does veneration relate to it?
premises: The object is fixed in full: all-pervading (vyāpta) particular of moving-and-unmoving states (carācarabhāvaviśeṣa), consisting of consciousness (cinmaya), one (eka), endless (ananta), beginningless (anādi).
The act follows: Bhairava-Lord (bhairavanātham), refuge of the helpless (anāthaśaraṇyaṃ), venerated by mind-become-Yours (tvanmayacittatayā), in heart (hṛdi) — vande (I venerate).
Veneration is not ritual offering but mental absorption: the devotee's mind becoming His (tvanmaya).

The name Bhairava performs its own nirukta here: bearing/supporting the universe, the Roar (rava) of AHAM, benefactor of the terrified — all three senses lived in the single act of absorption (Tantrāloka 1.95-100).
Total surrender is sized to its object: the all-pervading consciousness is venerated by absorption into it, not by offering to it.
bh-p01.inference: The Absolute is named in full, then venerated by absorption into it; the name is lived, not glossed. Veneration is not offering but becoming.
uncertainties: Whether 'carācarabhāvaviśeṣa' means particular states or the particularity of states is unresolved.
Whether 'anādi' negates temporal beginning only or all limitation is unresolved.
The nirukta is performed, not stated; the verse does not gloss its own name.

bh-p02.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person recognition)
bh-p02.question: How does the world appear as His, and how is identity declared?
premises: Disclosure first: all this (etad), become of You (tvanmayam), without remainder (aśeṣam), now (idānīm) appears (bhāti) to me (mama) — by the power of Your grace (tvadanugrahaśaktyā).
Then declaration: You (tvaṃ), Maheśa, always (sadaiva) my self (mamātmā); made of my own self (svātmamayaṃ), all (samastam) is mine (mama) through Him (tena).
Grace is the cause of both disclosure and declaration; merit is not.
Appearance, then ownership — the two-step is the pratyabhijñā structure.
uncertainties: Whether 'svātmamaya' means 'made of my self' or 'self-identical' is unresolved.
Whether 'tena' refers to grace or to Maheśa is unresolved.

bh-p03.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person recognition)
bh-p03.question: How can fear be denied while suffering is conceded?
premises: Fear-talk denied: with You as Lord (nāthe) pervading (viśvagaye) own self (svātmani), therefore (tena) no talk of transmigration-fear exists (na saṃsṛtibhītikathā asti).
Affliction conceded in the same breath: even though (satsvapi) hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karma-hosts.
No-fear and full-suffering together — the concession framed by the denial, resolved within the verse, not deferred.
The non-dual recognition does not deny affliction; it denies fear of it: suffering is real, fear of it is not, because there is no 'other' to fear.
bh-p03.inference: Fear-talk denied while suffering conceded: denial and concession in one breath, resolved within the verse.
uncertainties: Whether 'prāyeṇa' (mostly) softens the claim or qualifies it is unresolved.
Whether 'karmagaṇa' means masses of karma or hosts of karmic beings is unresolved.

bh-p04.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person prayer and declaration)
bh-p04.question: How does the devotee turn aside death's gaze?
premises: Prayer first: O Ender (antaka), do not (mā) direct (vinidhehi) toward me (māṃ prati) this (enām) most wrathful-terrible (krodhakarālatamām) gaze (dṛśam).
Then the ground: firm (dhīra) in Śaṅkara-service (sevana) and contemplation (cintana), filled (maya) with terrifying, awe-full Bhairava-power (bhīṣaṇabhairavaśakti) — asmi (I am).
Power first invoked against death's gaze, then declared as state.
Śaṅkara here = Śiva, not Śaṅkarācārya — the context of Bhairava-service requires it.
bh-p04.inference: Prayer first, then the ground: power declared as state, not begged. The devotee testifies to possessing power, grounded in service and contemplation.
uncertainties: Whether 'asmi' is a declaration of achieved state or a performative utterance is unresolved.
Whether 'śaṅkara' could refer to Śaṅkarācārya is resolved as Śiva by context.

bh-p05.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person fearlessness)
bh-p05.question: How does fearlessness follow from awareness?
premises: Great darkness already dispelled (dārita bhūri tamisra) by rays (dīdhiti) of awareness (saṃvid) consisting of world-becoming (bhavanmaya).
Then the catalogue — death, Yama, ender, karma-ghosts — met with salutation (namo 'stu) alone.
Never (na jātu) fear (bibhemi): awareness burned the dark before the terrors were named.
Salutation finishes what light began: the terrors are met with salutation, not weapons.
bh-p05.inference: Awareness first, salutation finishes: absolute fearlessness. The dark that made terrors terrifying is already gone.
uncertainties: Whether 'bhavanmaya' (world-becoming) modifies awareness or rays is unresolved.
Whether the four terrors are a complete list or exemplary is unresolved.

bh-p06.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person entry)
bh-p06.question: What does true awakening disclose, and what is bliss?
premises: Arisen (prodita) true (satya) awakening (vibodha): its rays (marīci) reveal (prekṣita) the true essence (satattva) of world-objects (viśvapadārtha).
On that ground — in You (tvayi), being-full (bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇa), I the self (aham ātmani) enter (emi) bliss (nirvṛtim).
Awakening discloses; entry is bliss; pūrṇa (full/complete) is the Lord's nature.
Bliss is ingress into fullness, not a feeling produced.
bh-p06.inference: Awakening discloses things as they are; bliss is entry into the Lord's fullness — ingress, not feeling.
uncertainties: Whether 'prodita' (arisen) modifies awakening or rays is unresolved.
Whether 'bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇa' is one compound or several is unresolved.

bh-p07.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person recognition)
bh-p07.question: What is the relation between affliction and nondifference?
premises: When indeed (yadaiva) the affliction-state (kleśadaśā), producing slight anguish (tanutāpavidhātrī), comes (eti) into the mind's range (mānasagocaram) —
— then alone (tadaiva) my nondifference with You (mama tvadabhedaḥ), and the rain of supreme nectar arises (stotraparāmṛtavṛṣṭir udeti).
Affliction's arrival dated as nondifference's occasion: with it, not after it, the nectar rains.
The verse inverts the expected: suffering is not the enemy of recognition but its trigger.
bh-p07.inference: Affliction is the occasion, not the obstacle: nondifference + nectar arise with it, not after it.
uncertainties: Whether 'tanutāpa' (slight anguish) is physical or mental is unresolved.
Whether 'yadaiva' is temporal or conditional is unresolved.

bh-p08.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person address)
bh-p08.question: What do rites and scripture each accomplish?
premises: Truly (satyam), O Śaṅkara: vow (vrata), giving (dāna), bathing (snāna), austerity (tapas) — dispels (vidāri) becoming's heat (bhavatāpa).
Rites relativized, not despised: heat dispelled by rites.
Contemplation (cintā) of Your (tāvaka) scripture (śāstra) as supreme nectar (parāmṛta), in mind (cetasi), streams (syandati) a bliss-stream (nirvṛtidhārā).
Heat dispelled by rites; bliss streamed by contemplation.
bh-p08.inference: Two means, two results: rites dispel heat, contemplation streams bliss.
uncertainties: Whether 'vadeśakālam' is obscure or means 'place-and-time under control' is unresolved.
Whether the rites are listed exhaustively or exemplarily is unresolved.

bh-p09.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person rejoicing)
bh-p09.question: What is obtaining, and who obtains?
premises: This consciousness of mine (saṃvid iyaṃ mama) dances (nṛtyati), sings (gāyati), deeply (gāḍham) rejoices (hṛṣyati) — O Bhairava-Lord.
Having obtained (āpya) You, the dear (priyam): the beautiful vision alone (sudarśanam ekam), hard to get by others (durlabham anyajanaiḥ).
Addressed to, and fenced to, the knower of the samaya (samayajña).
Joy first, then its cause named: obtaining = vision, rare by structure.
bh-p09.inference: Joy, then its cause: obtaining is vision, rare by structure and fenced to the initiated.
uncertainties: Whether 'samayajña' is vocative or qualifier converging on the same fence is unresolved.
Whether 'sudarśanam ekam' means 'the one beautiful vision' or 'beautiful vision alone' is unresolved.

bh-p10.speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person colophon)
bh-p10.question: What does the dated, signed hymn accomplish?
premises: In the month of Pauṣa, on the dark tenth, Abhinavagupta made this hymn: dated, signed.

By whom (yena) — devotee or hymn, undivided in effect — the pervasive (vibhuḥ), compassionate (dayāluḥ) Lord becomes (bhavati), pacifies (śamayati) the world's desert-heat of becoming — instantly (jhaṭiti).
The dated hymn turns outward: private recognition cools the world.
The verse moves from colophon to pacification to speed: inward dissolution (v.1) to world-pacification.
bh-p10.inference: Dated and signed: the hymn turns outward, private recognition cools the world.
uncertainties: Whether 'yena' refers to devotee or hymn is unresolved.
Whether 'bhavamarusantāpa' is physical or existential heat is unresolved.

bh-p01.plain_english: Pervading the particular states of moving and unmoving — consciousness-made, one, endless, beginningless: Bhairava-Lord, refuge of the helpless — by mind become Yours, in heart I venerate.
bh-p01.sanskrit_cite: vyāptacarācarabhāvaviśeṣam cinmayam ekam anantam anādim | bhairavanātham anāthaśaraṇyaṃ tvanmayacittatayā hṛdi vande

bh-p02.plain_english: All this, become of You, now appears to me by the power of Your grace. You, Maheśa, are always my self; by You all is mine.

bh-p03.plain_english: With You as Lord, all-pervading in own self — therefore no talk of transmigration-fear. Even though hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karmas are present.
bh-p03.sanskrit_cite: svātmani viśvagaye tvayi nāthe tena na saṃsṛtibhītikathā asti | satsvapi durdhara duḥkha vimoha trāsa vidhāyiṣu karmagaṇeṣu

bh-p04.plain_english: O Ender, turn not toward me this most wrathful-terrible gaze. Firm in Śaṅkara-service and contemplation, I am filled with terrifying Bhairava-power.

bh-p05.plain_english: Thus — great darkness dispelled by rays of world-awareness: death, Yama, the ender, karma-ghosts — Lord, salutation; never do I fear.

bh-p06.plain_english: The true essence of world-objects is seen by rays of arisen true awakening. In being-full in You — I, the self, enter bliss.

bh-p07.plain_english: When the affliction-state, producing slight anguish, comes into the mind's range — Lord, then alone is my nondifference with You; the supreme-nectar-rain arises.

bh-p09.plain_english: This consciousness of mine dances, sings, deeply rejoices — O Bhairava-Lord. Having obtained You, the dear: the beautiful vision alone, hard to get by others, samaya-knower.

bh-p10.plain_english: In the month of Pauṣa, on the dark tenth, Abhinavagupta made this hymn. The pervasive, compassionate Lord pacifies the world's desert-heat — instantly.
bh-p10.sanskrit_cite: vasurasapauṣe kṛṣṇadaśamyām abhinavaguptaḥ stavam imam akarot yena vibhuḥ bhavati janasya arusantāpaṃ śamayati jhaṭiti dayāluḥ

essence: Bhairava is established as all-pervading conscious reality: one, endless, beginningless — the Absolute that pervades moving and unmoving states.
The Lord is then venerated as refuge of the helpless by a mind become His — veneration as mental absorption, not ritual offering.
The nirukta of Bhairava (bearing/supporting, the Roar of AHAM, benefactor of the terrified) is here performed, not stated: the name is lived.
Total surrender is sized to its object — the all-pervading consciousness is venerated by absorption into it.

sections.SUMMARY: The Lord is established as all-pervading conscious reality — one, endless, beginningless — then venerated as refuge of the helpless by a mind become His.

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as veneration of all-pervading consciousness
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of veneration (vandana); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at consciousness pervading all. The rasa is not erotic or heroic but the tranquility of recognition beginning: the Absolute named, the devotee absorbed. Abhinava's own rasa theory (rasadhvani) is here the frame, not decoration — the verse aims at relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute, and the C1 names that relish.

essence: Grace first discloses the world as His, without remainder, now — then identity is declared outright: Maheśa, always my self, and all mine through Him.
Appearance, then ownership: grace showing the world as His before identity claims it.
The non-dual recognition (pratyabhijñā) is here performed as a two-step: disclosure, then declaration.

sections.SUMMARY: Grace first discloses the world as His; then identity declared outright: Maheśa, always my self — and all mine through Him.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at grace disclosing the world as His. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual identity, not the joy of acquisition — all is mine already, through Him.

essence: Fear-talk is denied while suffering is conceded: with You as Lord pervading own self, no talk of transmigration-fear.
Even though hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karmas stand — no-fear and full-suffering together, resolved within it, not deferred.
The non-dual recognition does not deny affliction; it denies fear of it.

sections.SUMMARY: Fear-talk denied while suffering conceded: no discussion of transmigration-fear, yet affliction stands granted — denial and concession in one breath.

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as no fear-talk, suffering conceded
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of fearless recognition; the vyabhicāri is concession (anukampa) of suffering without fear. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual recognition facing suffering — not the joy of denial but the peace of no-fear.

essence: Death's gaze is turned aside by prayer: O Ender, do not direct this wrathful-terrible gaze toward me.
The ground of the prayer: firm in Śaṅkara-service and contemplation, filled with terrifying Bhairava-power — asmi (I am).
Power first invoked against death's gaze, then declared as state. Śaṅkara here is Śiva, not Śaṅkarācārya.

sections.SUMMARY: Death's gaze turned aside by prayer; service and firm contemplation produce the power-filled state, testified with asmi — I am.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of prayer (prārthanā); the vyabhicāri is courage (dhairya) filled with Bhairava-power. The rasa is heroic, not tranquil — the devotee declares power against death's gaze. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as vīra: the sthāyibhāva of utsāha (energy) aimed at the Absolute.

essence: Darkness already burned away by awareness; four terrors then met with salutation alone, yielding absolute fearlessness.
Awareness burned the dark before the terrors were named; salutation finishes what light began.
It moves from accomplished fact (darkness dispelled) to catalogue (terrors) to response (salutation) to result (no fear).

sections.SUMMARY: Darkness already burned away by awareness; four terrors then met with salutation alone, yielding absolute fearlessness.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of fearlessness (abhaya); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at darkness dispelled. The rasa is the tranquility of no-fear, not the thrill of confrontation — the terrors are met with salutation, not defiance.

essence: True awakening discloses things as they are: its rays reveal the true essence of world-objects.
In You, being-full, I the self enter bliss — ingress, not feeling.
Awakening discloses; entry is bliss; pūrṇa (full/complete) is the Lord's nature.

sections.SUMMARY: True awakening discloses things as they are; bliss is entry into the Lord's fullness — ingress, not feeling.

rasa.sthayibhava: ānanda (bliss) as entry into the Lord's fullness
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of entry (praveśa); the vyabhicāri is bliss (ānanda) of awakening. The rasa is bliss as ingress, not as feeling — the devotee enters what the Lord already is.

essence: Affliction's arrival is the occasion, not the obstacle: with it comes nondifference, and nectar arises.
Affliction's arrival dated as nondifference's occasion: with it, not after it, the nectar rains.
It inverts the expected: suffering is not the enemy of recognition but its trigger.

sections.SUMMARY: Affliction's arrival is the occasion, not the obstacle: with it comes nondifference, and nectar arises.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of nondifference (abheda); the vyabhicāri is joy (harṣa) that affliction is the occasion. The rasa is the tranquility of recognition in suffering — not the joy of pain but the peace that suffering is not other.

essence: Rites are relativized: vow, giving, bathing, austerity dispel becoming's heat — while scripture contemplated as nectar irrigates the mind with a bliss-stream.
Heat dispelled by rites; bliss streamed by contemplation. Two means, two results.
Rites are not despised; they are relativized, then the higher means offered.

sections.SUMMARY: Rites relativized — vow, giving, bathing, austerity dispel heat — while scripture contemplated as nectar irrigates the mind with a bliss-stream.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of contemplation (cintā); the vyabhicāri is peace (śānti) of the bliss-streamed mind. The rasa is the tranquility of contemplation, not the austerity of rites.

essence: Consciousness dances and sings; obtaining the Lord is defined as rare vision — fenced to the initiated.
Joy first, then its cause named: obtaining = vision, rare by structure.
It moves from rejoicing to the definition of obtaining as vision, fenced to the knower of the samaya.

sections.SUMMARY: Consciousness dances and sings; obtaining the Lord is defined as rare vision — fenced to the initiated.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of rejoicing (hṛṣṭi); the vyabhicāri is joy (camatkāra) of obtaining the vision. The rasa is bliss as spontaneous joy, then defined as vision — not emotion but recognition.

essence: Dated and signed, it turns outward: the compassionate Lord pacifies the world's heat instantly.
What began in the heart ends in the world: private recognition cools the world.
The colophon dates the composition (Pauṣa, Kṛṣṇa Daśamī) and signs it (Abhinavagupta), then turns to the world.

sections.SUMMARY: Dated and signed, it turns outward: the compassionate Lord pacifies the world's heat instantly — what began in the heart ends in the world.

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as pacification of the world
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of pacification (śamana); the vyabhicāri is compassion (karuṇā) of the dated hymn. The rasa is the tranquility of compassion — the hymn that began in inward dissolution ends in world-pacification.

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as veneration of all-pervading consciousness; FIRST VERSE — sets the house voice (doctrine first, then the name; owner verdict required). Sanskrit-first: sthāvara-jaṅgama (moving AND unmoving — the pair IS the pervasion, kept paired); namāmi (I BOW — the verse's only act, kept last). Abhinavagupta frame: veneration as mental absorption (manasā bhūtvā — mind-become-His), not offering; the name lived, not glossed (argmap INF). Rows: 9 (moving/unmoving catalogue — pair kept bare), 7 (Bhairava-vocative mid-verse — address AFTER establishment; order IS the recognition: what, then whom), 1 (‘I bow’ end-weighted). Close: ‘in my heart, I bow’. Rupture: em-dash after ‘is one’ (all-pervasion stated, then the person enters). Rejected: ‘I prostrate’ — killed: contemporary diction (license ledger); fronting the vocative — killed: name-after-pervasion is the recognition performed; ‘refuge of helpless ones’ plural — killed: anātha kept singular-abstract (‘the helpless’). Read aloud: per-VAD-ing EV-ery STATE of MOV-ing and un-MOV-ing, CON-scious-ness it-SELF is ONE … BHAI-ra-va, LORD … IN-my-HEART, i-BOW.

Read aloud: ALL-this, be-COME-yours with-OUT re-MAIN-der … YOU, ma-HE-śa, are EV-er MY-own-SELF — MADE-of-you, ALL is MINE through-YOU.

reads_against.argmap: How does the world appear as His, and how is identity declared? → Recognition is two-step, not one.
c1_essence: Grace first discloses the world as His, without remainder, now — then identity is declared outright: Maheśa, always my self, and all mine through Him.
Appearance, then ownership: grace showing the world as His before identity claims it.
The non-dual recognition (pratyabhijñā) is here performed as a two-step: disclosure, then declaration.

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as no-fear-talk, suffering conceded (denial and concession in one breath). Sanskrit-first: vārtā (TALK/report — the verse denies the DISCOURSE of fear, not just the feeling); sati (STAND — suffering stands; fear does not). Rows: 9 (denial + concession held unreconciled — ‘no talk…Even while…’ never resolves, resolved WITHIN per C1), 1 (‘stand’ closes — sthā: what stands is named last), 7 (Lord-vocative L1 — pervasion stated TO him). Close: ‘karma-hosts stand’. Rupture: ‘Even while’ (denial turns to concession — the breath holds both). Rejected: ‘yet suffering remains’ — killed: duḥsaha (hard-to-BEAR) kept hard (Bar 6: never smooth); ‘no fear of rebirth’ — killed: saṃsāra-bhaya-vārtā is fear-talk; ‘hosts of karma’ reordering — killed: terror-causing kept fronted (bhayaṅkara modifies first). Read aloud: YOU, lord, per-VADE my OWN-self — SO there IS no TALK … EV-en WHILE hard-to-BEAR SUFF-er-ing … STAND.

reads_against.argmap: How can fear be denied while suffering is conceded? → Fear-talk denied while suffering conceded: denial and concession in one breath, resolved within the verse.
c1_essence: Fear-talk is denied while suffering is conceded: with You as Lord pervading own self, no talk of transmigration-fear.
Even though hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karmas stand — no-fear and full-suffering together, resolved within it, not deferred.
The non-dual recognition does not deny affliction; it denies fear of it.

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra as power-filled state (FIRST vīra in the work — color shift from śānta supplication to heroic testimony). Sanskrit-first: antaka (ENDer — death named to its face, kept); asmi (I AM — the ground is a state, not a plea); ghora-bhairava-tejas (dread-power, kept dread). Rows: 7 (‘O Ender’ opens — address before petition; death faced first), 1 (‘dread Bhairava-power’ closes — the state named last), 5 (prayer tread: plea L1, ground L2). Close: ‘filled with dread Bhairava-power’. Rupture: L2 (prayer turns to testimony — begging turns to possessing; argmap: power declared, not begged). Rejected: ‘awesome’ — killed: ghora is dread, awe admires; ‘fierce gaze’ — killed: raudra + bhīṣaṇa both present, both kept; ‘avert’ for ‘turn from me’ — killed: parāṅmukha kept bodily (turned-face). Read aloud: O-END-er — TURN-from-me THIS most-WRATH-ful AND-terr-i-BLE-gaze … STEAD-fast in ŚAṄ-ka-ra's SER-vice … i-AM-filled WITH-dread BHAI-ra-va-POW-er.

reads_against.argmap: How does the devotee turn aside death's gaze? → Prayer first, then the ground: power declared as state, not begged. The devotee testifies to possessing power, grounded in service and contemplation.
c1_essence: Death's gaze is turned aside by prayer: O Ender, do not direct this wrathful-terrible gaze toward me.
The ground of the prayer: firm in Śaṅkara-service and contemplation, filled with terrifying Bhairava-power — asmi (I am).
Power first invoked against death's gaze, then declared as state. Śaṅkara here is Śiva, not Śaṅkarācārya.

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as fearlessness (abhayam); accomplished-fact → catalogue → seal. Sanskrit-first: vidhūta (DISPELLED — perfect participle: already done before the terrors are named); namas (SALUTATION — the only act offered to terrors); na bhayaṃ (NEVER fear — absolute, future). Rows: 9 (Death/Yama/Ender/karma-ghosts — four terrors named, each answered by ONE salutation), 1 (‘never shall I fear’ closes — the seal absolute), 6 (salutation as seal-word — namas anchors). Close: ‘never shall I fear’. Rupture: colon after ‘rays’ (fact stated, then terrors faced — awareness first, salutation finishes per C1). Rejected: ‘darkness’ singular softening — killed: mahāmoha + bhava-grasp both kept; ‘I salute, fearing nothing’ — killed: splits the seal pair (namas + never-fear belong together); ‘gloom’ — killed: moha is delusion-darkness, gloom moods. Read aloud: THUS — the GREAT-dark-ness … IS-dis-PELLED by a-WARE-ness's-RAYS … DEATH, YA-ma, the END-er, KAR-ma-ghosts — LORD, sal-u-TA-tion: NEV-er SHALL-i-FEAR.

reads_against.argmap: How does fearlessness follow from awareness? → Awareness first, salutation finishes: absolute fearlessness. The dark that made terrors terrifying is already gone.
c1_essence: Darkness already burned away by awareness; four terrors then met with salutation alone, yielding absolute fearlessness.
Awareness burned the dark before the terrors were named; salutation finishes what light began.
It moves from accomplished fact (darkness dispelled) to catalogue (terrors) to response (salutation) to result (no fear).

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: ānanda as entry (praveśa — ingress, NOT feeling); vyabhicāri wonder at things disclosed as-they-are. Sanskrit-first: prabuddha (DAWNED-awakened — perfect: already risen); amṛta-pūrṇa (NECtar-FULL — pūrṇa modifies the LORD, kept attached); praviśāmi (I ENTER — first person enters, not feels). Rows: 1 (‘enter bliss’ closes — entry, the verse's whole doctrine, last), 8 (vowel arc bright throughout: dawn-rays-reveal → brimming-full — ānanda does not fall, it fills; no dark close), 7 declined — no vocative; locative ‘In You’ carries address. Close: ‘I myself enter bliss’. Rupture: colon after ‘essence’ (disclosure turns to entry — seeing turns to entering). Rejected: ‘I feel bliss’ — killed: ingress ≠ feeling (C1 explicit); ‘full of nectar’ reordering — killed: pūrṇa belongs to the Lord; ‘true nature’ for ‘true essence’ — killed: tattva kept essence. Read aloud: TRUE a-WAK-en-ing HAS-dawned — its RAYS re-VEAL … IN-you — BRIMM-ing-FULL of su-PREME-nec-tar — i-my-SELF EN-ter BLISS.

reads_against.argmap: What does true awakening disclose, and what is bliss? → Awakening discloses things as they are; bliss is entry into the Lord's fullness — ingress, not feeling.
c1_essence: True awakening discloses things as they are: its rays reveal the true essence of world-objects.
In You, being-full, I the self enter bliss — ingress, not feeling.
Awakening discloses; entry is bliss; pūrṇa (full/complete) is the Lord's nature.

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as nondifference arising (abheda WITH affliction, not after). Sanskrit-first: yadā…tadā (WHEN…THEN — hinge kept; with-it, not after-it per C1); kevalam (ALONE — then-ALONE: nondifference exclusive); varṣati (RAINS — the hymn rains, kept raining). Rows: 1 (‘rains supreme nectar’ closes — verb last, nectar the landing), 9 (when/then hinge — occasion, not obstacle), 10 (nectar left standing, no gloss). Close: ‘the hymn rains supreme nectar’. Rupture: ‘then alone’ (affliction turns to nondifference — suffering is the trigger per C1, inverted expectation kept). Rejected: ‘whenever troubles come’ — killed: ārti (affliction) + mind's-reach both precise; ‘showers’ — killed: colloquial, varṣa rains; ‘my oneness with You’ — killed: abheda is nondifference (kept technical). Read aloud: when-EV-er af-FLIC-tion … COMES with-IN the MIND's-reach — THEN a-LONE, lord, MY-non-DIFF-er-ence FROM-you: the HYMN-rains su-PREME-nec-TAR.

reads_against.argmap: What is the relation between affliction and nondifference? → Affliction is the occasion, not the obstacle: nondifference + nectar arise with it, not after it.
c1_essence: Affliction's arrival is the occasion, not the obstacle: with it comes nondifference, and nectar arises.
Affliction's arrival dated as nondifference's occasion: with it, not after it, the nectar rains.
It inverts the expected: suffering is not the enemy of recognition but its trigger.

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as rites relativized (not despised — relativized); two-means-two-results. Sanskrit-first: śamaka (DISPELLERS — rites' true result kept: heat dispelled, honored); cintā (CONTEMPLATING — the superior means is mental, kept); dhārā (STREAM-course — kept stream, not flood). Rows: 1 (‘bliss-stream in the mind’ closes — contemplation's result lands last, outshining by position), 9 (vow/giving/bathing/austerity — each rite named once, none adorned), 5 (didactic tread: concession L1, elevation L2). Close: ‘pours a bliss-stream in the mind’. Rupture: ‘But’ (rites turn to scripture — relativization hinged on one word). Rejected: ‘empty rites’ — killed: rites truly dispel heat; ‘flood’ — killed: dhārā courses; ‘holy writ’ for scripture — killed: śāstra kept plain (contemporary diction). Read aloud: TRU-ly, ŚAṄ-ka-ra — VOW, GIV-ing, BATH-ing, aus-TER-i-ty: they dis-PEL be-COM-ing's-HEAT … BUT con-TEM-plat-ing YOUR-scrip-ture … POURS a BLISS-stream IN the MIND.

reads_against.argmap: What do rites and scripture each accomplish? → Two means, two results: rites dispel heat, contemplation streams bliss.
c1_essence: Rites are relativized: vow, giving, bathing, austerity dispel becoming's heat — while scripture contemplated as nectar irrigates the mind with a bliss-stream.
Heat dispelled by rites; bliss streamed by contemplation. Two means, two results.
Rites are not despised; they are relativized, then the higher means offered.

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: ānanda as rejoicing consciousness (hṛṣṭi); vyabhicāri wonder at rarity fenced. Sanskrit-first: nṛtyati/gāyati (DANCES/SINGS — kept tripled with rejoices: joy in three verbs); samaya-vid (COVENANT-KNOWERS — fenced term kept fenced AND translated: fence is doctrine); durlabha (HARD-to-obtain — kept). Rows: 9 (dances/sings/rejoices triple — tripled joy), 7 (‘O Bhairava, Lord’ mid-verse — address INSIDE the dance, joy first), 1 (‘covenant’ closes — rarity fenced last). Close: ‘kept for knowers of the covenant’. Rupture: colon after ‘Lord’ (dancing turns to defining — joy, then what joy means: obtaining = vision per C1). Rejected: ‘my beloved’ — killed: priya kept plain; explaining samaya — killed: un-fencing would un-fence the doctrine; ‘rare’ alone — killed: ‘hard for others to obtain’ keeps the exclusivity structure. Read aloud: THIS-con-SCIOUS-ness OF-mine DAN-ces, SINGS, re-JOI-ces DEEP-ly — o-BHAI-ra-va, LORD: HAV-ing-WON-you, my-DEAR — a-SING-le BEAU-ti-ful VI-sion … KEPT for KNOW-ers OF the COV-e-nant.

reads_against.argmap: What is obtaining, and who obtains? → Joy, then its cause: obtaining is vision, rare by structure and fenced to the initiated.
c1_essence: Consciousness dances and sings; obtaining the Lord is defined as rare vision — fenced to the initiated.
Joy first, then its cause named: obtaining = vision, rare by structure.
It moves from rejoicing to the definition of obtaining as vision, fenced to the knower of the samaya.

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as pacification (praśama — the work's seal turned outward); vyabhicāri compassion (karuṇā) for the people's heat. Sanskrit-first: pauṣa/kṛṣṇadaśamī (dark-tenth kept — colophon dates kept honestly, L3-HANDCRAFT rule 5); śamayati (STILLS — same root as śānta: the last verb echoes the rasa); abhinavagupta-signed (signature kept — the hand named). Rows: 12 (śānta-fall for the WHOLE work: desert-heat → stills; the book ends cooling), 10 (Vasura/Pauṣa/dark-tenth left standing — date as image), 1 (‘becoming’ closes — bhava named at the very end: what the hymn pacifies, last). Close: ‘desert-heat of becoming’. Rupture: second dash (signature turns outward — heart to world per C1). Rejected: modernizing the date — killed: colophon honesty; ‘quenches’ — killed: śamayati stills/pacifies (rasa-echo kept); ‘the suffering world’ — killed: jana (people) kept plain. Read aloud: IN the va-SU-ra YEAR, in PAU-ṣa, ON the DARK-tenth — ab-hi-na-va-GUP-ta com-POSED this HYMN — BY-which … IN-a-FLASH STILLS the PEO-ple's DES-ert-HEAT of be-COM-ing.

reads_against.argmap: What does the dated, signed hymn accomplish? → Dated and signed: the hymn turns outward, private recognition cools the world.
c1_essence: Dated and signed, it turns outward: the compassionate Lord pacifies the world's heat instantly.
What began in the heart ends in the world: private recognition cools the world.
The colophon dates the composition (Pauṣa, Kṛṣṇa Daśamī) and signs it (Abhinavagupta), then turns to the world.
